caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1456 of 2001
lawyer:
Akram Hossain Amin, Advocate-on-Record— For the Petitioners. 
ABM Siddique, Advocate-on-Record— For Respondent Nos. 17-26. 
Not represented— Respondent Nos. 1-16, 27-201
parties:
Abul Kashem Howlader & ors  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Kasem Ali Khan and others  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title and correction of record of right in respect of suit land stating, inter cilia, that 12 annas share of Kayem Karsha Gour Kishore Howlader was recorded in Khewat No. 41/1 and 4 annas share of the said Kayam Karsha was recorded in Khewat No. 41/1, out of the 12 annas share of the Kayem Karsha as recorded in Khewat No. 41/2, share belonged to Kajem Howlader and 4 annas belonged to Sadan Howlader and the Kayem Karsha was recorded in Khewat No. 41/2 belonged to Samajuddin Howlader out of total quantity of 14.57 acres of land recorded in Khewat No. 41/1, 3.51 acres was khas land and out of total 5.43 acres of land in Khewat No. 41/2, 3.40 acres was the khas land and the remaining land of the respective Khewats were tenanted land which were recorded under khatian Nos. 266 to 270 in the name of tenants. That Kajem Howlader and Sadan Howlader owned and possessed 3.51 acres of land of Khewat No. 41/1 and Somojuddin Howlader possessed 3.40 acres of khas land of Khewat No. 41/2. The said 3.51 acres have been recorded in plot Nos. 2818, 2825, 2828, 2835 and 2844 and the said 3.40 acres of khas land have been recorded in plot Nos. 2842, 2864, 2865 and 2867. That on the death of Kajem Howlader his sons Abdul Kader, Abdul Jabbar, Abdul Wahed and Ahmed Howlader in collusion with the landlords got the entire lands of the aforesaid 2 (two) Khewats auction sold and they purchased the same with their own money and for their own benefit in the benami of Baser Sarder. They also fabricated a Mirash Ijara in (FD) respect of 12 annas share of the entire Kayem Karsha including the tenanted land. That plaintiffs predecessor Khalilur Rahman and his co-sharers went to pay rents when the Tahsilder told them about the auction sale and thereupon a fresh dispute arose between Abdul Kader Howlader and his brothers, on one hand and Khalilur Rahman, on the other hand. Thereupon, Abdul Kader and his brother purchased 12 annas share of the entire Kayem Karsha from the said Baser Sarder in the benami of Abdul Sheikh and Munar Khan by suppression of the facts of Mirash Ijara to Khalilur Rahman and others. And the plaintiffs' predecessor Khalilur Rahman and others purchased the remaining 4 annas share from Baser Sarder and thus came to a settlement inasmuch as the previous position in regard to share in the entire Kayem Karsha remained as it was. After some time, the fraudulent creation of Mirash Ijara became known and thereupon a quarrel arose between Khalilur Rahman and his sharers on one side and Abdul Kader and his brothers on the other side. To have an amicable settlement in the matter, all the parties viz., Abdul Kader and his brother and Khalilur Rahman and his other co-sharers, namely, Hachan Howlader and Yasin Howlader (the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-19) executed and registered a deed of partition dated 25-7-1928. In terms of the said deed of partition Abdul Kader Howlader and his brothers got the khas and tenanted lands of Khewat No. 41/1 and Khalilur Rahman Howlader and Yasin Howlader got the entire khas and tenanted lands of Khewat No. 4½ as usual disregarding the fraudulent Mirash Ijara and fraudulent auction sale and purchase in the name of Baser Sarder at first and in the name of Abdul Shaikh and Munar Khan subsequently by way of fraudulent and benami transaction. The above named benamder Baser Sarder, Abdul Sheik and Munar Khan never possessed any land of the 2(two) Khewats. But subsequently, Abdul Kader's son Hashem Howlader, the defendant No. 20, got the RS and SA Khatians recorded fraudulently in their name by suppression of the terms of partition deed. That subsequently, the defendant Nos. 20 to 51 and their predecessors and the defendant Nos. 59 to 115 brought Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 alleging that RS and SA record of the lands of Khewat Nos. 41/1 and 41/2 are wrong. In that suit Khalilur Rahman the plaintiffs predecessor and the defendants Nos. 1-19 were included as plaintiffs. But, as a matter of fact, the said Khalilur Rahman alias Ibrahim Howlader predecessor of the plaintiff, never signed the power and the plaint; that he did not know anything about the suit; the signatures in the plaint and power were forged. After the death of Khalilur Rahman during pendency of the suit his heirs including the plaintiffs are alleged to have been substituted. But as a matter of fact the plaintiff did not know anything about the suit, nor he signed any vokalatnama or any petition in that suit. The plaintiff was all along serving in Pakistan Air Force and he was posted throughout in West Pakistan from 1952 to 1964 and the plaintiff had all along been living in West Pakistan with his family from the year, 1956 to May, 1964 and during this period, he never came to the then East Pakistan; plaintiff's signatures in any documents of the suit, if there be any, were all forged and fabricated and the plaintiff had no knowledge about the suit. That once plaintiff's father Khalilur Rahman for securing the repayment of a debt, executed a Jaisudi-mortgage of 1.25 of 0.25 bighas of land of his share from the land of Khewat No. 41/2 in favour of Abdul Jabbar, Abdul Wohed, Abdul Kader Ahmed Howlader and Hashem Ali Howlader, the defendant No. 20. Accordingly, possession of the mortgage land was also in their favour and subsequently, Khalilur Rahman repaid the mortgage debt and the Mortgagor returned the mortgage deed with an endorsement to its back and delivered possession of the mortgage land back to Khalilur Rahman. That the direct allegation of the plaintiff is that defendant No. 20. Hashem Ali Howlader is a corrupt and shrewd person and he has forged the name of Khalilur Rahman as the plaintiff in the title suit in collusion and with the help of defendants secured ex parte decree in that suit. Thereafter, Miscellaneous case arose in the name of different persons but ultimately those cases were dismissed and the decree of the title suit remained unchallenged. Subsequently, it transpired that the said defendant No. 20, got a substitution petition filed in the suit in the name of the minor sons of Khalilur Rahman without bringing it to the knowledge of their natural guardian; all these are done by the defendant No. 20 by practicing fraud upon the Court. That thereafter another Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 was fraudulently instituted through defendant No. 61. Mokhtar Ali, and on suppression of all processes by practicing fraud on the Court the suit was dismissed collusively. So in spite of all the rehearing of the cases and the Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 which were fabricated, the decree of the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 remaining unchallenged in some of the above suits and rehearing cases the plaintiff was made a party and the summons were shown served upon him fraudulently although the plaintiff had been living in West Pakistan serving in the Air Force. That it is stated that the original Title Suit No. 18 of 1956 was filed in the First Court of Subordinate Judge and subsequently, the said Title Suit was transferred to the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge and renumbered as Title Suit No. 49 of 1958; Khalilur Rahman, the plaintiff predecessor or the plaintiff himself never signed any power or plaint nor they authorised anybody else to sign any such paper on their behalf nor the plaintiff even engaged the Lawyer Babu Pabitra Kumar Ghose nor the plaintiff authorised Mohammad Ismail or Saijuddin to present any power on his behalf; all the papers standing in the name of Khalilur Rahman and the plaintiff are forged, fraudulent and collusive. The written statement said to have been filed in the name of defendant Nos. 20-38 in Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 through Hachan Imam Chowdhury, Advocate, is also fraudulent, inasmuch as no contesting defendant could file a written statement of that nature. The plaintiff never engaged Mr Hachan Imam Chowdhury. All these were done fraudulently by the defendant No. 20 and he suppressed everything and kept the plaintiff ignorant about the matter all through. The defendant Nos. 20-115 never possessed the land of the Khewat No. 41/2 measuring 3.73 acres being the suit land which have been recorded in RS Khatian No. 265 and SA Khatian No. 619 and the plaintiff came to know about the impugned decree in the last part of Falgun 1372 BS. Then he procured all the necessary particulars and papers and brought this suit for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal is illegal, fraudulent, void ab initio, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 120 and 121 supported the plaintiff's case by filing written statement. The defendant No. 7, 10-13 and 52-56 also supported the plaintiffs case by filing written statement. Defendant Nos. 26-107 contested the case filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and barred by the principles of res judicata. Their further case is that all the statements made in the plaint are false; that summons/notice/process of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956. Title Suit No. 49 of 1958. Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959, Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1959 and Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 were not collusive and fraudulent nor were they suppressed as alleged by the plaintiff. Their further case is that Khalilur Rahman the plaintiff's father signed all the necessary papers of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956 and the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and after his death the plaintiff and his brother Ismail, the defendant No. 4 and others file application under their own signature for substitution. None of this signature were forged and fabricated; plaintiff's brother Ismail got the Vokalatnama presented on 21-5-1958 through Saijuddin Howlader, the defendant No. 20 against whom allegations of fraud, collusion and fabrication have been made in the plaint, was then serving in a High School of Bhola and he did not know about the institution of the suit or cases. Ainuddin Sheikh who was defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (defendant No. 19 in the present suit) filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1959 which was dismissed on contest on 13-7-1959. Thereafter, Dhola Bibi defendant No.1 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and (now defendant No. 116 in this suit), filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959 and it was also dismissed on 23-6-1960. In the said Miscellaneous Case the plaintiff and his brother along with their co-sharers and the defendant Nos. 20-38 together filed a solenama and Ismail; the plaintiff's brother, had also deposed for Dhola Bibi in the said Miscellaneous Case; Mokter Ali who was defendant No. 11 in the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (now defendant No. 61 in this suit) filed Title Suit No. 3, of 1961; in that suit the defendant Nos. 20-38 -including the present plaintiff filed a joint written statement for setting aside the decree and plaintiff's brother Ismail deposed in that suit. The defendant No. 20 also filed a separate written statement. But in none of the suits and cases the plaintiff's signatures were forged as alleged in the plaint. The defendant's further case is that plaintiff's allegation that he had all along been in West Pakistan from 1952-1964 is false. Their case is that Baser Sarder purchased the khas and tenanted land of the Khewat Nos. 41/1 and 41/2 and possessed it and thereafter he granted a Mirash Ijara to the extent of 12 annas share to Abdul Kader and others, the predecessors of defendant Nos. 20-44 by vinue of a patta dated 17-10-1911 and thereafter Abdul Sheikh and Munir Khan acquired 12 annas share of khas and tenanted lands of the Kayem Karsha and Khalilur Rahman and others acquired the remaining 4 annas share. It is further alleged that on auction purchasing the Mirash Ijara recorded in Khatian No. 270 for arrears of rent, these defendants got the same merged in the Kayem Karsha and have been possessing as such a land of 6.91, 3.51 in total 10.42 acres appertaining to the khas land of Mirash Ijara as well as Kayem Karsha. These 10.42 acres subsequently increased to 10.60 acres. In short, these defendants have denied the allegation of the plaint and that Baser Sarder, Abdul Shiekh and Munir Khan were benamders. They also denied the deed of partition and they also raised an objection regarding the maintainability of this suit without impleading the heirs of the principal defendants in the suit. They have further denied that Sadan Howlader or his heirs did not possess any land on the basis of kabala from Abdul Shaikh and Munir Khan.
